title: Call for Publishers: Comma Journal – Request for Proposals
content:
The International Council on Archives (ICA) is inviting proposals from publishers interested in publishing Comma, its leading serial publication and a key benefit for ICA members. Comma is an international, multilingual journal covering the professional administration and development of archives and archivists worldwide. It aims to reach the widest possible global readership.

Comma usually publishes two themed issues per year. Its content includes contributions from ICA Congresses and Conferences, reports and studies based on the work of ICA Regional Branches, Professional Sections and Expert Groups, and special thematic issues. The Comma Editorial Board, comprising international archival professionals representing the ICA’s regions, oversees publication planning, themes and content.

The full Request for Proposals provides further details on publishing and distribution arrangements, requirements for future publishers, and administrative information.

Submission deadline: Friday 8 January 2027, at 23:59 CET (Paris time).

Download the full request for proposals.

title: CFP: ARCHIVES*RECORDS 2027
content:
ARCHIVES*RECORDS 2027 will take place August 25–28 at the Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk in Chicago, Illinois. The meeting will be held in person, bringing together archivists and allied professionals from across the country and around the world to connect, share knowledge, and explore the opportunities and challenges facing our profession.

Archivists have always done our best work together. We share expertise, lend a hand across institutions, and build what no single repository could build alone. Our work reaches well beyond the reading room: We help society remember its history, account for itself, and imagine what comes next. As our profession faces real challenges, community matters more than ever. The SAA Annual Meeting is a chance to gather, learn from one another, and look ahead with purpose and optimism.

title: CFP: Caribbean Records Series
content:
The Editorial Board of the Caribbean Records Series invites proposals and preliminary enquiries for scholarly publications that advance the study of Caribbean history through the recovery, editing, and publication of historical sources.

Published by the Jamaican Historical Society in collaboration with Open Book Publishers, the series builds on the Society’s commitment, since its founding in 1943, to preserving Jamaican and wider Caribbean history through the publication of historical records.

The series primarily publishes scholarly editions of primary sources relating to the history of the English-speaking Caribbean, broadly defined and spanning all periods. It also welcomes proposals for calendars of primary sources, historical dictionaries and encyclopedias, gazetteers, archaeological reports, and other scholarly reference works.

title: CFP: SAA Visual Materials Section 2027 Win-Ventory
content:
“Winventory” is fast approaching!

VMS invites archivists to share their work wins with our community as part of “Winventory’s” series of 5-7 minute lightning talks this coming January.

This year has been a difficult one, marked by uncertainty, change, and ongoing challenges across our communities and institutions. We hope to create a space to share some of our wins, encouraging reflection, creativity, connection, and resilience. We would love to see what made you pause, smile, or say “this is why I do this.”

Don’t know where to start? Here are some ideas:

• A visual materials project that brought people together

• A win (big or small) that came out of working with visual content

• A collaboration engaging between archive and artist

• A surprising visual discovery that brought a moment of joy

• A behind-the-scenes story from the stacks

• A successful digitization or outreach initiative

Submit your idea by November 20th! Please send proposals – a brief paragraph sharing your lighting talk idea – or any questions to Maggie McCready at mgmc@loc.gov!

title: CFP: Mid-Atlantic Regional Archives Conference Spring 2027
content:
Full details: https://www.marac.info/2027-spring-pittsburgh

To honor Pittsburgh’s distinct and vibrant neighborhoods as well as its history as the home of the Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood television series, the Program Committee invites proposals related to the theme Won’t You Be My Neighbor? Stronger Together. We are seeking proposals that highlight the many different skills, abilities, and backgrounds that enrich our archives, MARAC, and adjacent professions. This could include highlighting ways that communities and archives work together for the greater good as well as ways we can reach across any divides separating our internal and external neighborhoods and communities, whether they be ideological, budgetary, technological, geographical, educational, or otherwise.

The deadline for proposals is 5pm Monday, November 16, 2026. If you are looking for co-presenters or a moderator, consider posting to the Collaboration Spreadsheet. Spreadsheet entries are not proposal submissions and will not be considered. Please use the Submission Form to submit proposals.

title: CFP: Northwest Archivists at 50
content:
NWA Annual Meeting 2027
Helena, Montana

May 19-21, 2027

The 2027 NWA Annual Meeting gives us an opportunity to gather, collaborate, and learn from the work of archivists and other cultural heritage professionals from around our region. Our 2027 meeting will be held at the Montana Heritage Center in Helena, Montana. Our theme is Northwest Archivists at 50 in recognition of the golden anniversary of our professional organization.

Anniversaries offer the opportunity to look toward the future of our profession by reflecting on our past. Our work stewarding the past teaches us that knowing where we have been informs where we are going. In celebrating this anniversary, NWA seeks to reflect on the past 50 years of archival work, highlight collections in our region, and envision where we want to go next.
